newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court sentences former minister to jail.
newsitem.headline: Indian court sentences former minister to jail.

text.p: An Indian court trying cases under an anti-terrorist law sentenced a former government minister to 10 years in prison on Monday on charges of sheltering six people wanted by police, court officials said.

Kalpnath Rai, food minister in the previous Congress party government headed by Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, had been convicted of harbouring members of an alleged underworld gang believed to be linked to a string of bomb blasts in Bombay in March 1993 that killed 260 people.
He was also fined one million rupees ($27,932).

"The judge has to be sensitive to the social environment and cry of the society for justice. The gravity of the crime of accused Kalpnath Rai is much more than that of other ordinary criminals," Judge S.N. Dhingra said in his sentencing order.
Rai, who has denied the charges, said he would appeal against the order in a higher court.
"I have faith in court. I have faith in the judicial system of India and I have done nothing wrong. I would pray to god for justice," Rai said after hearing the order.
"I will definitely appeal against this order," he said.
About 50 of Rai's supporters shouted slogans in his defence as he was led out of the courtroom.

Rai was elected to parliament in May last year after campaigning from a jail cell. He stood as an independent after rebelling against Rao and his Congress party, which earlier refused to allow him to campaign under the party's banner.
Rai was released on bail just after voting.
Rai was tried under the Terrorist And Disruptive Activities Act (TADA), a law scrapped in 1995 after heavy criticism from human rights activists, who considered it draconian.
Cases started when the law was in force are still being tried under it.
Rai was convicted of sheltering members of a Bombay gang led by Dawood Ibrahim, who has been named by government investigators as the suspected mastermind of the 1993 bombings.
Ibrahim, a fugitive abroad, has denied the charges in secret media interviews.
